items.q: What happens when you let agents 'end-to-end everything'?
items.a: You get **thousands of flaky E2E tests**, even on a **simple CRUD app**. Decide what you are testing and **trim**.

items.q: Why does waiting on an agent wreck focus?
items.a: A 10–20 minute wait tempts you to start **more concurrent tasks**, and by three or four you are **lost in the sauce**.

items.q: What should you do with 'if you're not doing X, you won't make it'?
items.a: **Ignore that person.** Agent workflows **change in weeks**, so the specific X is already stale.
Use the messy first AI pass as a **prototype to learn the shape**, then **redesign a tighter V2** of the same features.

items.q: What did that loop do to Prime's Oligarchy prototype?
items.a: Same features, better shape, about **100k lines down to 25–30k**, and the feeling that **he made it**.

items.q: Who should you refuse to become when coding with AI?
items.a: A **prompt proxy** who only relays intent into a box and **merges whatever comes back**.

items.q: Why do juniors have the shortest stick in the AI era?
items.a: They must **move like seniors** because the tool looks senior, but they never get to **learn what good looks like**.

items.q: How does the model handle a junior's bad idea?
items.a: It **does not push back**. It hands over a **thousand-line PR** 'how you asked.'
The person who **thinks through tests, layout and trade-offs**, not the one who is only a **relay into a text box**.
